findings.title: Rejected devices are cached as successfully admitted
findings.body: TagDevice now propagates the device-limit error to authentication, but tagDeviceUI still inserts the device into localCache before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice. When the store rejects a new device because the limit is reached, that cache entry remains for 29 minutes. A second request with the same device ID hits the cache, returns nil, and is authenticated anonymously despite the limit. Cache a device only after a successful store operation, and add a test that retries a rejected device.

findings.title: Device admission uses a non-atomic count-then-insert
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice counts active devices in one database session and performs the upsert separately, without locking or an atomic admission operation. If the count is one below the limit, concurrent requests with different new device IDs can all observe the available slot and all insert successfully. This also occurs across Grafana instances sharing the database, so the configured limit can be exceeded persistently. Serialize admission at the database level and cover concurrent admissions in a test.

findings.title: Omitting the device header bypasses the anonymous limit
findings.body: Authenticate enforces the limit only when TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, but TagDevice returns nil immediately when X-Grafana-Device-Id is missing. An unauthenticated client can therefore omit this client-controlled header and continue receiving an anonymous identity and accessing protected APIs even when the configured device limit is exhausted. Admission needs a server-enforced device-identification path, or equivalent enforcement for requests without this header, rather than relying on clients voluntarily supplying it.
